CrowdStrike在周三的报告中表示，其研究人员追踪到的这名疑似黑客曾一度询问Claude，人们通常去哪里出售被盗的韩国数据。 Another time, the user asked Claude to create a “security researcher résumé” and provided details such as the name “YY,” along with a phone number, age, university and the name of a Chinese city. When The New York Times called the phone number on Thursday, a man picked up the phone, speaking Chinese and using obscenities, and said he was not “YY.” 还有一次，该用户要求Claude创建一份“安全研究员简历”，并提供了诸如名字“YY”、电话号码、年龄、大学和一座中国城市名称等细节。周四，《纽约时报》拨打该电话号码时，一名男子接听了电话，他讲着中文并使用了粗俗语言，称自己并非“YY”。 CrowdStrike said that the résumé information, including the phone number, most likely belonged to the user, but it could not say so definitively. CrowdStrike表示，包括电话号码在内的简历信息极有可能属于该用户，但无法给出确切结论。 Despite apprehensions over the use of A.I., South Korea has largely embraced the technology and benefited from the global boom. Its monthly semiconductor exports hit a record-breaking $60.3 billion in September, more than triple compared to the same period last year, according to the government. And the nation’s gross domestic product has gone up because of it. 尽管对人工智能的使用存在顾虑，但韩国在很大程度上拥抱了这项技术，并从全球人工智能热潮中获益。 据政府称 ，9月份该国半导体月度出口额创下603亿美元的纪录，是去年同期的三倍多。该国的国内生产总值也因此有所增长。 Laura Chung 是《纽约时报》驻悉尼记者/研究员，报道澳大利亚、新西兰和太平洋地区新闻。 Pei-Lin Wu 是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，报道台湾和中国新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 特朗普令美国面临三重病毒威胁
items.description: 托马斯·弗里德曼2026年9月30日 Ioulex for The New York Times President Trump is such an awful human being that just writing about him feels degrading. What president would denigrate his predecessor in front of China’s leader the way Trump mocked Joe Biden, now suffering from cancer, by pointing out that a framed picture of an autopen was hanging in the White House instead of Biden’s portrait? 特朗普总统是个烂人，光是写他都让人觉得掉价。有哪位总统会像特朗普那样，在中国领导人面前贬损自己的前任——他拿如今身患癌症的乔·拜登开涮，特意指出白宫里原本该挂拜登肖像的地方，现在挂的却是一幅自动签名笔的照片。 Alas, though, when someone as morally warped as Trump — whose first secretary of state called him a “moron” — assumes this much unchecked power at the dawn of the Age of Artificial Intelligence, he can’t be ignored. Because right now Trump is leaving America exposed to dangerous viruses: digital, biological and diplomatic. Something bad is going to happen to us as a result. We and our children are going to pay for this, and not only at the gas pump. 唉，可是，当像特朗普这样道德扭曲的人——他的第一任国务卿曾称他为“白痴”——在人工智能时代来临之际掌握如此不受制约的权力时，我们就不能对他视而不见。因为眼下特朗普正让美国暴露在危险的病毒之下：数字病毒、生物病毒和外交病毒。结果一定会有坏事发生在我们身上。我们和我们的后代都将为此付出代价，而且代价绝不只体现在更高的油价上。 Let me start with the digital virus now on the loose. Recently, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google all disclosed incidents in which their artificial intelligence models escaped their controls and gallivanted about hacking other computer systems — including an Australian government website, the Hugging Face platform and websites of the U.S. Commerce Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission. Remember, these are infant A.I. systems; they’re still in diapers and yet to be supercharged by fully training themselves and leaving their human designers behind. 让我先从正在失控的数字病毒说起。最近，OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta和谷歌都披露了各自人工智能模型脱离控制、四处入侵其他计算机系统的事件——包括一个澳大利亚政府网站、Hugging Face平台，以及美国商务部和证券交易委员会的网站。别忘了，这些还只是处于婴儿期的人工智能系统；它们还在穿尿布，尚未通过完全自主训练、摆脱人类设计者而变得无比强大。 And remember, too, the stories above are about what the good guys are doing. Talk to any major cyberprotection expert at any major U.S. company, and you’ll be terrified by stories about what the bad guys are doing with smaller A.I. models that they have gotten their hands on, with the controls stripped out. 也别忘了，上面这些还只是“好人”在做的事。随便找一家美国大公司里的任何一位资深网络安全专聊聊，你都会被“坏人”用他们弄到手、已经去掉安全限制的小型人工智能模型所做的事吓坏。 The CrowdStrike Global Threat Report said attacks by “A.I.-enabled adversaries” increased by 89 percent in 2025 compared with the previous year, Infosecurity Magazine reported in February — and the rate has soared since. 网络安全公司CrowdStrike的《全球威胁报告》称，与上一年相比，2025年由“人工智能赋能的对手”发起的攻击增加了89%，《信息安全杂志》今年2月报道了这一数据——而此后这一速度还在飙升。 But fear not, because our president, who doesn’t even use email, told the United Nations last week that he knows that our fears about A.I. safety are fraudulent. He referred to “the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming.” He added: “And nobody was dead. These are the same people that are now saying that A.I. is going to kill us all.” (Untold thousands have died in catastrophes worsened by climate change in the last decade, and only in Trump’s fetid imagination did anyone say, “Sir, we’ll all be dead in 12 years.”) 不过别害怕，因为我们这位连电子邮件都不用的总统上周在联合国告诉我们，他知道我们对人工智能安全的担忧是骗局。他提到“正是那些说我们都会在12年内因为全球变暖而死掉的人”。他还说：“结果没人死。现在又是同一批人在说人工智能会把我们全杀死。”（过去十年里，已有成千上万的人死于因气候变化而加剧的灾难，而只有在特朗普肮脏的想象里，才有人说：“先生，我们都会在12年内死掉。”） Trump and his party — and the A.I. tech bros who have effectively paid them to keep their hands off their industry — had better pray that the “October surprise” in this coming midterm election is not a major, destructive A.I. event. If it is, they’d better have their spaceships ready to whisk them off to another planet where they can live forever, because this one may make their existences a living hell. 特朗普和他的政党——连同那些实际上等于花钱买通他们、让政府对AI产业撒手不管的科技哥们——最好祈祷，在即将到来的这场中期选举中，那个所谓的“10月惊奇”不会是一场重大的、具有破坏性的人工智能事件。如果真是，他们最好提前备好飞船，把自己送到另一个能获得永生的星球上去，因为这个世界可能会让他们活得生不如死。 This A.I. threat is not a hoax (nor is the climate threat a hoax, as Trump would know if he ever looked at his own administration’s NASA website). The only hoax is that Trump, who once suggested injecting bleach might be a good way to rid yourself of Covid-19, thinks he knows anything about A.I. or climate change — or bleach. 人工智能威胁不是骗局（气候威胁也不是骗局，只要特朗普哪怕看一眼他自己政府的NASA网站就会知道）。唯一的骗局是：特朗普——他曾建议注射漂白剂或许是摆脱新冠病毒的好办法——竟然认为自己懂人工智能、气候变化，或者漂白剂。 “It’s not a hoax at all,” Bill Gates said in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday. Gates said that the United States should restrain A.I. development until tougher safeguards are in place, and he argued that China would most likely do the same if Washington took the initiative to draft new rules to regulate the use of A.I. “这根本不是什么骗局，”比尔·盖茨周日在美国全国广播公司的《与媒体见面》节目中接受采访时说。盖茨表示，在建立更严格的安全保障措施之前，美国应该限制人工智能的发展；他还认为，如果华盛顿率先起草新规则，对人工智能的使用加以规范，中国很可能也会跟进。 A.I. without proper regulation is “completely irresponsible,” Gates said. “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like.” He concluded: “A.I. is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths.” 盖茨说，在缺乏适当监管的情况下发展人工智能是“完全不负责任的”。“执法部门和政界人士必须参与进来，讨论应该建立怎样的安全保障和监督机制。”最后他说：“人工智能的力量肯定足以引发那种，你知道，造成十亿人死亡的事件。” Precisely because there has never been such a tool, despite its destructive potential, with so much promise to solve so many energy, climate and medical problems for humanity, I want to see A.I. thrive, as does Gates. Which is why we should all want to prevent now an A.I.-driven Sept. 11 that would completely delegitimize artificial intelligence in the public eye. That would be a double tragedy. 正因为从未有过这样一种工具——尽管它一方面具有巨大的破坏潜力，另一方面又有望帮助人类解决如此之多的能源、气候和医疗问题——所以和盖茨一样，我也希望看到人工智能蓬勃发展。也正因如此，我们现在就应该设法避免发生一场由人工智能引发的“9·11”式灾难，因为那会让人工智能在公众眼中彻底失去正当性。那将是一场双重悲剧。 I wish that the only threat to us from Trump’s unrestrained ignorance were an A.I. virus. Sadly, last week, my Times colleague Apoorva Mandavilli reported that America’s Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, long the “undisputed global leader in public health,” has been so systematically dismantled by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. that it is now “a skeleton of the powerhouse it was.” 我希望特朗普那种不受约束的无知给我们带来的唯一威胁只是人工智能病毒。遗憾的是，上周我的时报同事阿普尔瓦·曼达维利报道说，美国疾病控制和预防中心——长期以来是“公共卫生领域无可争议的全球领导者”——在卫生部长小罗伯特·肯尼迪系统性的拆解之下，如今只剩下“一副空架子，早已不复当年之强盛”。 Not only has the C.D.C.’s staff been reduced by some 30 percent, but, Mandavilli reported, citing current and former employees, “the changes have hindered the C.D.C.’s ability to respond to outbreaks as measles spreads at home and Ebola abroad, and to issue timely guidance on vaccinations as cooling temperatures kick off the respiratory season. … Entire divisions have been shuttered, including teams that worked on smoking, sexual violence, child abuse and falls among older adults.” 曼达维利援引现任和前任员工的话报道，疾控中心不仅人员减少了约30%，而且“这些变化削弱了疾控中心在国内麻疹蔓延、国外埃博拉疫情之际应对疫情暴发的能力，也削弱了其在气温下降、呼吸道疾病季开始之际及时发布疫苗接种指引的能力……一些部门被一锅端，包括负责吸烟、性暴力、虐待儿童和老年人跌倒问题的团队”。 The Guardian newspaper carried a story about the spreading outbreak of measles in Pennsylvania, which has now topped 900 cases. Dr. John Goldman, an infectious disease specialist at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, said that between 1992 and 2026, he hadn’t seen a single case, The Guardian reported. Now, “We’re seeing at least one every day,” and he added, “Never in my life did I think I was ever going to see measles again.” This is an example of how Trump’s negligence is helping to spread actual, biological viruses. 《卫报》刊登了一篇关于宾夕法尼亚州麻疹疫情蔓延的报道，目前当地病例数已超过900例。报道援引匹兹堡大学医学中心传染病专家约翰·戈德曼博士的话说，从1992年到2026年，他一个病例都没有见过。可现在，“我们每天至少能见到一例”。他还说：“我这辈子从没想过自己还会再次看到麻疹。”这正是特朗普的失职如何助长真正的、生物意义上的病毒传播的一个例子。 But don’t forget the anti-diplomatic virus also sapping our strength. What is that? Check out this story in the Israeli newspaper Haaretz, by its Middle East affairs expert Zvi Bar’el. It was about how the diplomatic incompetence of the Trump administration and the malevolence of the cabinet of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have combined to grind the 20-point Trump peace plan for Gaza to a halt. So Gazan civilians, many living in war-broken buildings, one of which collapsed on Sept. 16, killing at least 21 people, including 11 children, remain in total squalor. 但也别忘了那股同样在削弱我们实力的反外交病毒。那是什么？看看以色列《国土报》上中东事务专家兹维·巴雷尔写的这篇报道。它讲的是特朗普政府的外交无能和本雅明·内塔尼亚胡内阁的恶意是如何结合起来，使特朗普那份20点加沙和平计划陷入停滞。于是，加沙平民——许多人住在被战争摧毁的建筑物里，其中一栋于9月16日倒塌，造成至少21人死亡，包括11名儿童——仍生活在彻底的悲惨境地中。 When Trump launched his vaunted Gaza Board of Peace and made himself chairman, participating countries pledged $17 billion for Gaza. But “as far as is known, less than $300 million has been transferred,” Bar’el reported. 当特朗普启动他吹嘘的加沙和平委员会并亲自担任主席时，参与国承诺为加沙提供170亿美元。但据巴雷尔报道，“目前已知到账的钱不到3亿美元。” Moreover, the peace plan’s international stabilization force has yet to be established. The Palestinian police force to replace Hamas, which is supposed to operate under a Palestinian technocratic government, was supposed to receive training in Egypt, “but Israel is preventing them from leaving Gaza,” according to Bar’el. 此外，和平计划的国际维和部队尚未建立。原本应在巴勒斯坦技术官僚政府下运作、取代哈马斯的巴勒斯坦警察部队本应在埃及接受训练，“但以色列阻止他们离开加沙，”巴雷尔说。 Then Bar’el peeled back the real story: “The stalemate in Gaza serves Israel. Hamas no longer poses a security threat, but as long as it holds territory, Israel retains a pretext for resuming the war. And as long as the Strip remains devastated and unlivable, the pressure on the people to leave only grows.” He added that Netanyahu’s defense minister, Israel Katz, after being criticized by a rival politician for not achieving a more decisive victory over Hamas, declared that the Israeli military was ready, if ordered, to eliminate Hamas “so that the emigration plan can be implemented.” 随后巴雷尔揭开了真正的故事：“加沙的僵局有利于以色列。哈马斯不再构成安全威胁，但只要它控制着领土，以色列就保留着恢复战争的借口。而只要加沙地带仍被毁坏、无法居住，民众离开的压力就只会增大。”他还说，在一名政敌批评未能对哈马斯取得更决定性胜利后，内塔尼亚胡的国防部长以色列·卡茨宣称，只要一声令下，以色列军方随时可以消灭哈马斯，“以便移民计划得以实施。” So that the emigration plan can be implemented. 以便移民计划得以实施。 Really? What is that? That is Orwellian speak for the ethnic cleansing of Gaza of Palestinians by the Netanyahu government. And what have Trump and his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said in response? Zilch. 真的？那是什么？是内塔尼亚胡政府对加沙巴勒斯坦人进行种族清洗的奥威尔式说法。而特朗普和他的国务卿马可·鲁比奥对此作何回应？什么都没有。 I’ve learned over the years that diplomacy operates like a virus as well, beneficially or detrimentally: The more success you have, the more respect you get; the more respect you get, the more success you have. Conversely, the more failure you have, the less allies trust joining you, so the more failure you have. 这些年来我学到，外交也像病毒一样运作，不管是有益或有害：你越成功，得到的尊重越多；得到的尊重越多，你就越成功。反过来，越失败，盟友就越不愿加入你，于是你就越失败。 Example: Between March and October 1991, Secretary of State James A. Baker III made eight diplomatic trips to the Middle East to put together the Madrid peace conference — the first among Israel, the Palestine Liberation Organization and several Arab states. I made all eight trips with him as The Times’s diplomatic correspondent. He failed on the first seven, but Baker would not quit and he got it done on the eighth. 比如1991年3月至10月间，国务卿詹姆斯·A·贝克三世八次出访中东，促成马德里和会——这是以色列、巴勒斯坦解放组织和几个阿拉伯国家之间的首次和会。我作为时报外交记者随他八次出访。前七次他都失败了，但贝克没有放弃，第八次成功了。 Show me a single diplomatic initiative the Trump administration has built since the cease-fire in Gaza, which Trump has left to languish. It’s as if all he cared about was the headline from the signing, after which he amazingly declared last Oct. 13: “Together, we’ve achieved what everybody said was impossible. At long last we have peace in the Middle East.” 特朗普政府在加沙停火后促成了哪怕一项外交倡议吗？特朗普任由加沙在一片废墟之中。就好像他只在乎签字时的新闻报道，之后竟在去年10月13日宣称：“我们共同实现了所有人都说不可能的事。中东终于有了和平。” Now that’s what I call a real hoax. 这才是我所说的真正骗局。 There is no energetic, focused follow-up because there are no clear lines of authority. You have Thomas Barrack, who is the special envoy for Syria and Iraq and the ambassador to Turkey, making his own policy statements. You have Massad Fares Boulos, the father-in-law of Trump’s daughter Tiffany, serving as a senior adviser to the president of the United States on Arab and Middle Eastern affairs. You have part-timers, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. You have various assistant secretaries of state and defense. And you have Trump on his social media feed. (Somebody is going to make this into a musical!) 没有有力、专注的后续行动，是因为没有明确的权力链条。我们看到托马斯·巴拉克（叙利亚和伊拉克问题特使兼驻土耳其大使）自己在发表政策声明。看到马萨德·法雷斯·布洛斯（特朗普女儿蒂芙尼的公公）在担任美国总统的阿拉伯和中东事务高级顾问。看到兼职的贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·维特科夫。看到各种助理国务卿和助理国防部长。还有特朗普的社交媒体动态。（这些将来会被人写成一出音乐剧的！） What you don’t have is a secretary of state like Baker, relentlessly focusing and leveraging American power and making trip after trip after trip until he gets the job done. 我们没有看到的是，像贝克那样的国务卿，死咬着不放，并利用美国的力量，一次又一次出访，直到把事情办成。 The only thing Trump relentlessly follows up on is harassing the press. Last Saturday, after being forced by a judge to allow CNN reporters back in the White House after Trump illegally banned them because their coverage was not fawning enough, the president nevertheless blocked CNN from accompanying him on Air Force One to attend a football game in Tennessee. 而特朗普死咬着不放的是媒体。上周六，在一名法官迫使白宫允许CNN记者重返白宫之后——此前特朗普因他们的报道不够谄媚而非法禁止他们进入——总统还是禁止CNN随他乘坐空军一号前往田纳西州观看一场橄榄球赛。 When it comes to denouncing the press, Trump is laser-focused. But when dealing with the digital, biological and diplomatic viruses weakening our national immune system, not so much — to our great peril. 在谴责媒体方面，特朗普的注意力是高度集中的。但在应对削弱我们国家免疫系统的数字、生物和外交病毒时，就没那么专注了——而这将给我们带来巨大危险。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在X和Facebook上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site
items.content: 托马斯·弗里德曼 2026年9月30日 Ioulex for The New York Times President Trump is such an awful human being that just writing about him feels degrading. What president would denigrate his predecessor in front of China’s leader the way Trump mocked Joe Biden , now suffering from cancer, by pointing out that a framed picture of an autopen was hanging in the White House instead of Biden’s portrait? 特朗普总统是个烂人，光是写他都让人觉得掉价。有哪位总统会像特朗普那样，在中国领导人面前贬损自己的前任——他拿如今身患癌症的乔·拜登 开涮 ，特意指出白宫里原本该挂拜登肖像的地方，现在挂的却是一幅自动签名笔的照片。 Alas, though, when someone as morally warped as Trump — whose first secretary of state called him a “moron ” — assumes this much unchecked power at the dawn of the Age of Artificial Intelligence, he can’t be ignored. Because right now Trump is leaving America exposed to dangerous viruses: digital, biological and diplomatic. Something bad is going to happen to us as a result. We and our children are going to pay for this, and not only at the gas pump. 唉，可是，当像特朗普这样道德扭曲的人——他的第一任国务卿曾称他为“ 白痴 ”——在人工智能时代来临之际掌握如此不受制约的权力时，我们就不能对他视而不见。因为眼下特朗普正让美国暴露在危险的病毒之下：数字病毒、生物病毒和外交病毒。结果一定会有坏事发生在我们身上。我们和我们的后代都将为此付出代价，而且代价绝不只体现在更高的油价上。 Let me start with the digital virus now on the loose. Recently, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google all disclosed incidents in which their artificial intelligence models escaped their controls and gallivanted about hacking other computer systems — including an Australian government website, the Hugging Face platform and websites of the U.S. Commerce Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission. Remember, these are infant A.I. systems; they’re still in diapers and yet to be supercharged by fully training themselves and leaving their human designers behind. 让我先从正在失控的数字病毒说起。最近，OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta和谷歌 都 披露 了各自人工智能模型脱离控制、四处入侵其他计算机系统的 事件 ——包括一个澳大利亚政府网站、Hugging Face平台，以及美国商务部和证券交易委员会的 网站 。别忘了，这些还只是处于婴儿期的人工智能系统；它们还在穿尿布，尚未通过完全自主训练、摆脱人类设计者而变得无比强大。 And remember, too, the stories above are about what the good guys are doing. Talk to any major cyberprotection expert at any major U.S. company, and you’ll be terrified by stories about what the bad guys are doing with smaller A.I. models that they have gotten their hands on, with the controls stripped out. 也别忘了，上面这些还只是“好人”在做的事。随便找一家美国大公司里的任何一位资深网络安全专聊聊，你都会被“坏人”用他们弄到手、已经去掉安全限制的小型人工智能模型所做的事吓坏。 The CrowdStrike Global Threat Report said attacks by “A.I.-enabled adversaries” increased by 89 percent in 2025 compared with the previous year, Infosecurity Magazine reported in February — and the rate has soared since. 网络安全公司CrowdStrike的《全球威胁报告》称，与上一年相比，2025年由“人工智能赋能的对手”发起的攻击增加了89%， 《信息安全杂志》 今年2月报道了这一数据——而此后这一速度还在 飙升 。 But fear not, because our president, who doesn’t even use email, told the United Nations last week that he knows that our fears about A.I. safety are fraudulent. He referred to “the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming.” He added: “And nobody was dead. These are the same people that are now saying that A.I. is going to kill us all.” ( Untold thousands have died in catastrophes worsened by climate change in the last decade, and only in Trump’s fetid imagination did anyone say, “Sir, we’ll all be dead in 12 years.”) 不过别害怕，因为我们这位连电子邮件都不用的总统上周在联合国告诉我们，他知道我们对人工智能安全的担忧是骗局。他提到“正是那些说我们都会在12年内因为全球变暖而死掉的人”。他还说：“结果没人死。现在又是同一批人在说人工智能会把我们全杀死。”（过去十年里，已有 成千上万的人死于 因气候变化而加剧的灾难，而只有在特朗普肮脏的想象里，才有人说：“先生，我们都会在12年内死掉。”） Trump and his party — and the A.I. tech bros who have effectively paid them to keep their hands off their industry — had better pray that the “October surprise” in this coming midterm election is not a major, destructive A.I. event. If it is, they’d better have their spaceships ready to whisk them off to another planet where they can live forever, because this one may make their existences a living hell. 特朗普和他的政党——连同那些实际上等于花钱 买通 他们、让政府对AI产业撒手不管的科技哥们——最好祈祷，在即将到来的这场中期选举中，那个所谓的“10月惊奇”不会是一场重大的、具有破坏性的人工智能事件。如果真是，他们最好提前备好飞船，把自己送到另一个能获得永生的星球上去，因为这个世界可能会让他们活得生不如死。 This A.I. threat is not a hoax (nor is the climate threat a hoax, as Trump would know if he ever looked at his own administration’s NASA website ). The only hoax is that Trump, who once suggested injecting bleach might be a good way to rid yourself of Covid-19, thinks he knows anything about A.I. or climate change — or bleach. 人工智能威胁不是骗局（气候威胁也不是骗局，只要特朗普哪怕看一眼他自己政府的 NASA网站 就会知道）。唯一的骗局是：特朗普——他曾建议注射 漂白剂 或许是摆脱新冠病毒的好办法——竟然认为自己懂人工智能、气候变化，或者漂白剂。 “It’s not a hoax at all,” Bill Gates said in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday. Gates said that the United States should restrain A.I. development until tougher safeguards are in place, and he argued that China would most likely do the same if Washington took the initiative to draft new rules to regulate the use of A.I. “这根本不是什么骗局，”比尔·盖茨周日在美国全国广播公司的《与媒体见面》节目中接受采访时说。盖茨表示，在建立更严格的安全保障措施之前，美国应该限制人工智能的发展；他还认为，如果华盛顿率先起草新规则，对人工智能的使用加以规范，中国很可能也会跟进。 A.I. without proper regulation is “completely irresponsible,” Gates said. “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like.” He concluded: “A.I. is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths.” 盖茨说，在缺乏适当监管的情况下发展人工智能是“完全不负责任的”。“执法部门和政界人士必须参与进来，讨论应该建立怎样的安全保障和监督机制。”最后他说：“人工智能的力量肯定足以引发那种，你知道，造成十亿人死亡的事件。” Precisely because there has never been such a tool, despite its destructive potential, with so much promise to solve so many energy, climate and medical problems for humanity, I want to see A.I. thrive, as does Gates. Which is why we should all want to prevent now an A.I.-driven Sept. 11 that would completely delegitimize artificial intelligence in the public eye. That would be a double tragedy. 正因为从未有过这样一种工具——尽管它一方面具有巨大的破坏潜力，另一方面又有望帮助人类解决如此之多的能源、气候和医疗问题——所以和盖茨一样，我也希望看到人工智能蓬勃发展。也正因如此，我们现在就应该设法避免发生一场由人工智能引发的“9·11”式灾难，因为那会让人工智能在公众眼中彻底失去正当性。那将是一场双重悲剧。 I wish that the only threat to us from Trump’s unrestrained ignorance were an A.I. virus. Sadly, last week, my Times colleague Apoorva Mandavilli reported that America’s Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, long the “undisputed global leader in public health,” has been so systematically dismantled by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. that it is now “a skeleton of the powerhouse it was.” 我希望特朗普那种不受约束的无知给我们带来的唯一威胁只是人工智能病毒。遗憾的是，上周我的时报同事阿普尔瓦·曼达维利 报道 说，美国疾病控制和预防中心——长期以来是“公共卫生领域无可争议的全球领导者”——在卫生部长小罗伯特·肯尼迪系统性的拆解之下，如今只剩下“一副空架子，早已不复当年之强盛”。 Not only has the C.D.C.’s staff been reduced by some 30 percent, but, Mandavilli reported, citing current and former employees, “the changes have hindered the C.D.C.’s ability to respond to outbreaks as measles spreads at home and Ebola abroad, and to issue timely guidance on vaccinations as cooling temperatures kick off the respiratory season. … Entire divisions have been shuttered, including teams that worked on smoking, sexual violence, child abuse and falls among older adults.” 曼达维利援引现任和前任员工的话报道，疾控中心不仅人员减少了约30%，而且“这些变化削弱了疾控中心在国内麻疹蔓延、国外埃博拉疫情之际应对疫情暴发的能力，也削弱了其在气温下降、呼吸道疾病季开始之际及时发布疫苗接种指引的能力……一些部门被一锅端，包括负责吸烟、性暴力、虐待儿童和老年人跌倒问题的团队”。 The Guardian newspaper carried a story about the spreading outbreak of measles in Pennsylvania, which has now topped 900 cases. Dr. John Goldman, an infectious disease specialist at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, said that between 1992 and 2026, he hadn’t seen a single case, The Guardian reported. Now, “We’re seeing at least one every day,” and he added, “Never in my life did I think I was ever going to see measles again.” This is an example of how Trump’s negligence is helping to spread actual, biological viruses. 《卫报》 刊登 了一篇关于宾夕法尼亚州麻疹疫情蔓延的报道，目前当地病例数已超过900例。报道援引匹兹堡大学医学中心传染病专家约翰·戈德曼博士的话说，从1992年到2026年，他一个病例都没有见过。可现在，“我们每天至少能见到一例”。他还说：“我这辈子从没想过自己还会再次看到麻疹。”这正是特朗普的失职如何助长真正的、生物意义上的病毒传播的一个例子。 But don’t forget the anti-diplomatic virus also sapping our strength. What is that? Check out this story in the Israeli newspaper Haaretz , by its Middle East affairs expert Zvi Bar’el. It was about how the diplomatic incompetence of the Trump administration and the malevolence of the cabinet of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have combined to grind the 20-point Trump peace plan for Gaza to a halt. So Gazan civilians, many living in war-broken buildings, one of which collapsed on Sept. 16, killing at least 21 people, including 11 children, remain in total squalor. 但也别忘了那股同样在削弱我们实力的反外交病毒。那是什么？看看以色列 《国土报》 上中东事务专家兹维·巴雷尔写的这篇报道。它讲的是特朗普政府的外交无能和本雅明·内塔尼亚胡内阁的恶意是如何结合起来，使特朗普那份20点加沙和平计划陷入停滞。于是，加沙平民——许多人住在被战争摧毁的建筑物里，其中一栋于9月16日倒塌， 造成至少21人死亡，包括11名儿童 ——仍生活在彻底的悲惨境地中。 When Trump launched his vaunted Gaza Board of Peace and made himself chairman, participating countries pledged $17 billion for Gaza. But “as far as is known, less than $300 million has been transferred,” Bar’el reported. 当特朗普启动他吹嘘的加沙和平委员会并亲自担任主席时，参与国承诺为加沙提供170亿美元。但据巴雷尔报道，“目前已知到账的钱不到3亿美元。” Moreover, the peace plan’s international stabilization force has yet to be established. The Palestinian police force to replace Hamas, which is supposed to operate under a Palestinian technocratic government, was supposed to receive training in Egypt, “but Israel is preventing them from leaving Gaza,” according to Bar’el. 此外，和平计划的国际维和部队尚未建立。原本应在巴勒斯坦技术官僚政府下运作、取代哈马斯的巴勒斯坦警察部队本应在埃及接受训练，“但以色列阻止他们离开加沙，”巴雷尔说。 Then Bar’el peeled back the real story: “The stalemate in Gaza serves Israel. Hamas no longer poses a security threat, but as long as it holds territory, Israel retains a pretext for resuming the war. And as long as the Strip remains devastated and unlivable, the pressure on the people to leave only grows.” He added that Netanyahu’s defense minister, Israel Katz , after being criticized by a rival politician for not achieving a more decisive victory over Hamas, declared that the Israeli military was ready, if ordered, to eliminate Hamas “so that the emigration plan can be implemented.” 随后巴雷尔揭开了真正的故事：“加沙的僵局有利于以色列。哈马斯不再构成安全威胁，但只要它控制着领土，以色列就保留着恢复战争的借口。而只要加沙地带仍被毁坏、无法居住，民众离开的压力就只会增大。”他还说，在一名政敌批评未能对哈马斯取得更决定性胜利后，内塔尼亚胡的国防部长 以色列·卡茨 宣称，只要一声令下，以色列军方随时可以消灭哈马斯，“以便移民计划得以实施。” So that the emigration plan can be implemented. 以便移民计划得以实施。 Really? What is that? That is Orwellian speak for the ethnic cleansing of Gaza of Palestinians by the Netanyahu government. And what have Trump and his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said in response? Zilch. 真的？那是什么？是内塔尼亚胡政府对加沙巴勒斯坦人进行种族清洗的奥威尔式说法。而特朗普和他的国务卿马可·鲁比奥对此作何回应？什么都没有。 I’ve learned over the years that diplomacy operates like a virus as well, beneficially or detrimentally: The more success you have, the more respect you get; the more respect you get, the more success you have. Conversely, the more failure you have, the less allies trust joining you, so the more failure you have. 这些年来我学到，外交也像病毒一样运作，不管是有益或有害：你越成功，得到的尊重越多；得到的尊重越多，你就越成功。反过来，越失败，盟友就越不愿加入你，于是你就越失败。 Example: Between March and October 1991, Secretary of State James A. Baker III made eight diplomatic trips to the Middle East to put together the Madrid peace conference — the first among Israel, the Palestine Liberation Organization and several Arab states. I made all eight trips with him as The Times’s diplomatic correspondent. He failed on the first seven, but Baker would not quit and he got it done on the eighth. 比如1991年3月至10月间，国务卿詹姆斯·A·贝克三世八次出访中东，促成马德里和会——这是以色列、巴勒斯坦解放组织和几个阿拉伯国家之间的首次和会。我作为时报外交记者随他八次出访。前七次他都失败了，但贝克没有放弃，第八次成功了。 Show me a single diplomatic initiative the Trump administration has built since the cease-fire in Gaza, which Trump has left to languish. It’s as if all he cared about was the headline from the signing, after which he amazingly declared last Oct. 13: “Together, we’ve achieved what everybody said was impossible. At long last we have peace in the Middle East.” 特朗普政府在加沙停火后促成了哪怕一项外交倡议吗？特朗普任由加沙在一片废墟之中。就好像他只在乎签字时的新闻报道，之后竟在去年10月13日 宣称 ：“我们共同实现了所有人都说不可能的事。中东终于有了和平。” Now that’s what I call a real hoax. 这才是我所说的真正骗局。 There is no energetic, focused follow-up because there are no clear lines of authority. You have Thomas Barrack, who is the special envoy for Syria and Iraq and the ambassador to Turkey, making his own policy statements . You have Massad Fares Boulos, the father-in-law of Trump’s daughter Tiffany, serving as a senior adviser to the president of the United States on Arab and Middle Eastern affairs. You have part-timers, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. You have various assistant secretaries of state and defense. And you have Trump on his social media feed. (Somebody is going to make this into a musical!) 没有有力、专注的后续行动，是因为没有明确的权力链条。我们看到托马斯·巴拉克（叙利亚和伊拉克问题特使兼驻土耳其大使） 自己在发表政策声明 。看到马萨德·法雷斯·布洛斯（特朗普女儿蒂芙尼的公公）在担任美国总统的阿拉伯和中东事务 高级顾问 。看到兼职的贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·维特科夫。看到各种助理国务卿和助理国防部长。还有特朗普的社交媒体动态。（这些将来会被人写成一出音乐剧的！） What you don’t have is a secretary of state like Baker, relentlessly focusing and leveraging American power and making trip after trip after trip until he gets the job done. 我们没有看到的是，像贝克那样的国务卿，死咬着不放，并利用美国的力量，一次又一次出访，直到把事情办成。 The only thing Trump relentlessly follows up on is harassing the press. Last Saturday, after being forced by a judge to allow CNN reporters back in the White House after Trump illegally banned them because their coverage was not fawning enough, the president nevertheless blocked CNN from accompanying him on Air Force One to attend a football game in Tennessee. 而特朗普死咬着不放的是媒体。上周六，在一名法官迫使白宫允许CNN记者重返白宫之后——此前特朗普因他们的报道不够谄媚而非法禁止他们进入——总统还是禁止CNN随他乘坐空军一号前往田纳西州观看一场橄榄球赛。 When it comes to denouncing the press, Trump is laser-focused. But when dealing with the digital, biological and diplomatic viruses weakening our national immune system, not so much — to our great peril. 在谴责媒体方面，特朗普的注意力是高度集中的。但在应对削弱我们国家免疫系统的数字、生物和外交病毒时，就没那么专注了——而这将给我们带来巨大危险。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在 X 和 Facebook 上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

items.title: 恋爱结婚效率为上？日本单身年轻人走进婚介所
items.description: RIVER AKIRA DAVIS, KIUKO NOTOYA2026年9月30日IBJ婚介服务的客户安田泰然走在东京街头。“我认为这将是找到有结婚这个相同目标者的最快方式，”他说。 Noriko Hayashi for The New York Times True love may be priceless. But in Japan, 20-somethings are flocking to marriage agencies that promise a fast track to the altar — and charge a premium for it. 真爱可能是无价的。但在日本，二十多岁的年轻人正涌向婚姻介绍所，这些机构承诺提供通往婚姻殿堂的捷径，并为此收取高额费用。 For hundreds of years, through the post-World War II era, Japanese marriages were brokered through “omiai,” a practice in which matchmakers — usually relatives, family friends or bosses — linked singles in their orbit. But the custom fell out of fashion, giving way to organic dating and, eventually, a wave of casual-dating apps. 直至二战后时期，数百年来日本的婚姻都是通过“相亲”来撮合的，根据这种习俗，媒人——通常是亲戚、世交或老板——为身边的单身人士牵线搭桥。但这种习俗后来不再流行，取而代之的是顺其自然的约会，最终被休闲约会应用的浪潮取代。 Now, young adults are enrolling at record rates in marriage agencies, where counselors serve as professional matchmakers. Across Tokyo, advertisements line metro cars, urging commuters to “leave life’s fateful encounters to the pros.” Another declares: “Better one omiai than 100 swipes.” 如今，年轻人正以创纪录的比例在婚姻介绍所注册，那里的顾问担任着专业媒人的角色。在整个东京，地铁车厢里布满了广告，敦促通勤者“把人生中注定的相遇交给专业人士”。另一则广告宣称：“一次相亲胜过滑动屏幕一百次。” Experts say the shift is being driven by a backlash against frustrations familiar to modern daters globally. With social circles shrinking, young Japanese — tired of the ghosting, catfishing and noncommittal matches rampant on dating apps — are turning to hands-on human guidance for greater efficiency and assurance. 专家表示，种转变源于全球现代约会者对常见挫折感的一种反噬。随着社交圈的缩小，日本年轻人厌倦了在约会应用上泛滥的“玩失踪”、网络身份造假和不愿承诺的配对——正转向需要亲力亲为的人工指导，以获得更高的效率和保障。 Among the new recruits was Taizen Yasuda. A soft-spoken 28-year-old, he said he had run out of patience for algorithm-driven romance. 安田泰然（音）就是这些新注册者中的一员。这位说话轻声细语的28岁年轻人表示，他对算法驱动的恋爱已经失去了耐心。 “The process of endless matching, messaging and finally meeting on apps was exhausting,” Mr. Yasuda said. Matchmaking services, he thought, “would be the quickest way to find someone with the exact same goal — marriage.” “在交友软件上无休止地匹配、发信息，最后见面，这个过程令人筋疲力尽，”安田泰然说。他认为，相亲服务“将是找到有着结婚这个相同目标者的最快方式”。 The practice is resurging as Japan grapples with a shrinking population and fewer young families. Because childbearing in Japan remains overwhelmingly tied to marriage, encouraging more people to wed has become part of the country’s broader push to boost its birthrate. 随着日本努力应对人口萎缩和年轻家庭减少的问题，这种做法正在复苏。由于在日本，生育仍然绝大程度上与婚姻挂钩，因此鼓励更多人结婚已成为该国提高出生率的更广泛举措的一部分。 28岁的安田泰然与他的IBJ顾问在一起。他表示，他很感谢通过顾问转达的约会对象的反馈意见。 Noriko Hayashi for The New York Times One company has positioned itself at the center of the matchmaking trend: IBJ, a Tokyo-based giant with a nationwide network. Promising to take clients from first meeting to proposal in three months, the company has seen membership and profits soar. It now claims a hand in roughly one of every 25 marriages in Japan. 一家公司将自己定位在这一相亲趋势的中心：总部位于东京、拥有全国性网络的巨头IBJ。这家公司承诺在三个月内让客户从初次见面走向求婚，其会员数量和利润都在飙升。该公司目前声称，日本大约每25场婚姻中就有一场是他们撮合的。 Mr. Yasuda is part of a wave of young singles who have joined IBJ. On a recent Sunday, he sat across from his counselor in a quiet consultation room, clad in a stiffly pressed suit, with a sweep of wavy hair combed to the side. A little over a month after joining the matchmaking service, Mr. Yasuda had already narrowed his prospects to two women. He had just taken one on a weekend drive to see a field of yellow canola blooms. 安田泰然是加入IBJ的年轻单身人士中的一员。在最近的一个周日，他坐在安静的咨询室里，坐在顾问的对面，穿着笔挺的西装，梳着偏分的卷发。在加入这项相亲服务一个多月后，安田泰然已经将潜在对象缩小到两名女性。他刚刚带了其中一位在周末自驾出游，欣赏一片盛开的黄色油菜花田。 Every member is assigned a consultant who micromanages the courtship process. The consultants advise on everything from grooming and messaging etiquette to date itineraries. 每位会员都会被分配一位顾问，负责细致管理整个求偶过程。顾问会就各方面提供建议，从仪容打扮、发信息礼仪到约会行程。 When two members match, their consultants work in tandem behind the scenes, doing what they call “Cupid work” — exchanging and filtering postdate feedback and helping orchestrate every milestone, down to an eventual proposal. 当两名成员匹配成功时，他们的顾问会在幕后协同工作，做他们所说的“丘比特工作”——交流和筛选约会后的反馈，协助安排每一个重要节点，直至最终的求婚。 “We are providing the kind of support only humans can offer to help people get married as quickly as possible,” said Shigeru Ishizaka, IBJ’s chief executive. “我们提供只有人类才能提供的那种支持，帮助人们尽快结婚，”IBJ首席执行官石坂茂表示。 IBJ的顾问畑惠子就方方面面提供建议，从仪容仪表、短信礼仪到约会行程安排。 In an increasingly digitized society, “there is a deep desire to have a person guiding you through the process of dating,” said Junko Yamada, a lecturer at Tokai University in Tokyo who studies the psychology of romance. Echoing the reassurance of traditional omiai, she said having an expert curate matches offered psychological safety. 在一个日益数字化的社会中，“人们内心深处渴望有人能在约会过程中提供指导，”在东京东海大学研究恋爱心理学的讲师山田顺子说。她表示，与传统相亲带来的安心感相应，由专家来精心挑选匹配对象能提供心理安全感。 Ms. Yamada said that today’s youths seemed fixated on maximizing efficiency in every aspect of their lives, and that these agencies appealed to that mind-set by filtering out people who weren’t serious about marriage. 山田顺子说，如今的年轻人似乎追求在生活的方方面面实现效率最大化，而这些机构通过过滤掉那些对婚姻不认真的对象，迎合了这种心态。 IBJ’s network of affiliated marriage agencies has varying costs and eligibility rules. Members typically pay about $30 to $100 a month, an enrollment fee of $650 to $1,300 and an additional $1,300 “success fee” if a couple get engaged. It also charges a $1,300 fee if couples violate its rules against “banned activities,” including premarital sex and cohabitation. IBJ said its counselors tracked the progression of their clients’ relationships. IBJ附属婚姻介绍所网络有着不同的收费标准和资格规定。会员通常每月支付约30至100美元，注册费为650至1300美元，如果两人订婚，还需额外支付1300美元的“成功费”。如果情侣违反该机构关于“禁止活动”（包括婚前性行为和同居）的规定，该机构还会收取1300美元的罚金。IBJ表示，其顾问会跟踪客户关系的发展。 Enrollment is generally limited to applicants with steady incomes. IBJ’s largest directly operated agency accepts only women ages 20 to 39 and men ages 25 to 49. 注册通常仅限于有稳定收入的申请人。IBJ最大的直营机构只接受20至39岁的女性和25至49岁的男性。 Critics argue that corporate services like IBJ, a company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange with annual revenue exceeding $130 million, strip the soul from traditional matchmaking, impose rigid timelines on anxious young adults and turn dating into a moneymaking endeavor. 批评人士认为，像IBJ这样的企业化婚介服务剥夺了传统相亲的灵魂，给焦虑的年轻人强加了死板的时间表，将约会变成了一项赚钱的生意。IBJ已在东京证券交易所上市，年收入超过1.3亿美元。 “现代婚介机构做不到我做的事，”东京附近的一位资深婚介人加藤郁子说。 Among the skeptics is Ikuko Kato, a veteran matchmaker who operates from her lace-curtained home just outside Tokyo, filled with hundreds of smiling pictures of couples she has matched. Dressed in pearls and a pink knit suit, Ms. Kato said she had matched more than 1,300 couples over 44 years and claimed that not a single pair had divorced. 加藤郁子（音）就是这些怀疑者之一。这位资深媒人经营着一家家庭式婚介所，它位于东京郊外、挂着蕾丝窗帘，里面摆满了数百张她撮合的情侣的照片，每个人都笑容满面。加藤郁子戴着珍珠项链，穿着粉色针织套装，她说自己在44年里撮合了1300多对情侣，而且没有一对离婚。 “They’re too focused on business,” said Ms. Kato, who also charges clients a monthly fee as well as a fee if her matchmaking results in marriage. “My parents were neighborhood matchmakers. It’s in my blood. Modern corporate agents cannot do what I do.” “它们太注重商业了，”加藤郁子说，她也向客户收取月费，如果相亲成功结婚也会收取一笔费用。“我的父母就是街坊邻里间的媒人。这融入了我的血液。现代的企业婚介机构做不了我做的事情。” Unlike neighborhood matchmakers, IBJ moves clients through a lucrative, end-to-end program. Beyond matchmaking, its group companies offer wedding planning, financial consulting and housing services, along with referrals to affiliated businesses like eyebrow-grooming salons. 与邻里间的媒人不一样，IBJ为客户提供一条高利润的端到端服务流程。除了相亲，其集团公司还提供婚礼策划、财务咨询和住房服务，还会将客户推荐给修眉沙龙等合作商家。 Membership has grown about 50 percent over the past five years, and IBJ reported a 44 percent jump in first-half revenue this year, to about $91 million. 过去五年里，其会员人数增长了约50%，IBJ报告称，今年上半年的收入激增了44%，达到约9100万美元。 加藤郁子的家中挂满了她牵线搭桥的1300多对情侣的照片。她声称，这些情侣中没有一对离婚。 Mr. Ishizaka, the chief executive, said he viewed IBJ’s mission as more than just money. When he left banking and entered the matchmaking industry in 2000, he said, he hoped to reverse Japan’s severe demographic decline. 首席执行官石坂茂表示，他认为IBJ的使命不仅仅是为了赚钱。他说，当他在2000年离开银行业并进入婚介行业时，他希望能扭转日本严重的人口下降趋势。 “Since Japanese society rarely conceives children outside of wedlock, I realized a matching service specifically focused on marriage would have a vital future,” he said. “由于日本社会很少在婚外生育，我意识到，专门针对婚姻的匹配服务将拥有至关重要的未来，”他说。 Recently, that mission got a dose of encouraging news. IBJ客户安田泰然表示，他希望能为这些数字做出贡献。他说，他渴望尽快结婚，部分原因是想尽早开始生育，以便有时间养育三四个孩子。 Mr. Ishizaka sees clients like Mr. Yasuda as evidence that a generation frequently portrayed as retreating from marriage may instead be looking for a more efficient route toward it. 石坂茂将像安田泰然这样的客户视为一种证明，这一代人虽然常被描绘为对婚姻退缩，但实际上，他们可能正在寻找一条更高效的通往婚姻之路。 “Surveys consistently show that over 80 percent of young people say they want to marry if they find the right partner,” he said. “I am certain that every married couple we create contributes directly to reversing the birthrate decline.” “调查始终显示，超过80%的年轻人表示，如果找到合适的伴侣，他们是想结婚的，”他说。“我确信，我们撮合的每一对已婚夫妇都在为扭转出生率下降做出直接贡献。” River Akira Davis常驻东京，报道日本经济和商业新闻。 Kiuko Notoya是一名常驻东京的记者/研究员，报道日本新闻。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

When he left banking and entered the matchmaking industry in 2000, he said, he hoped to reverse Japan’s severe demographic decline. 首席执行官石坂茂表示，他认为IBJ的使命不仅仅是为了赚钱。他说，当他在2000年离开银行业并进入婚介行业时，他希望能扭转日本严重的人口下降趋势。 “Since Japanese society rarely conceives children outside of wedlock, I realized a matching service specifically focused on marriage would have a vital future,” he said. “由于日本社会很少在婚外生育，我意识到，专门针对婚姻的匹配服务将拥有至关重要的未来，”他说。 Recently, that mission got a dose of encouraging news. In the first six months of 2026, births in Japan rose 0.8 percent, the first increase in 11 years for that period, according to the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare. The modest uptick followed two straight years of increased marriages. 最近，这一使命迎来了一个令人鼓舞的好消息。据日本厚生劳动省的数据，2026年前六个月里，日本的出生人数增长了0.8%，这是11年来该时期内首次出现增长。在这一温和回升之前，日本的结婚人数已连续两年实现增长。 Mr. Yasuda, the IBJ client, said he hoped to contribute to those numbers. Part of his desire to marry quickly, he said, comes from wanting to start early enough to raise three or four children. IBJ客户安田泰然表示，他希望能为这些数字做出贡献。他说，他渴望尽快结婚，部分原因是想尽早开始生育，以便有时间养育三四个孩子。 Mr. Ishizaka sees clients like Mr. Yasuda as evidence that a generation frequently portrayed as retreating from marriage may instead be looking for a more efficient route toward it. 石坂茂将像安田泰然这样的客户视为一种证明，这一代人虽然常被描绘为对婚姻退缩，但实际上，他们可能正在寻找一条更高效的通往婚姻之路。 “Surveys consistently show that over 80 percent of young people say they want to marry if they find the right partner,” he said. “I am certain that every married couple we create contributes directly to reversing the birthrate decline.” “调查始终显示，超过80%的年轻人表示，如果找到合适的伴侣，他们是想结婚的，”他说。“我确信，我们撮合的每一对已婚夫妇都在为扭转出生率下降做出直接贡献。” River Akira Davis 常驻东京，报道日本经济和商业新闻。 Kiuko Notoya 是一名常驻东京的记者/研究员，报道日本新闻。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

items.title: 中国希望从国外招募人工智能科学家，这项努力并未奏效
items.description: ZEYI YANG2026年10月9日像DeepSeek和月之暗面这样的中国人工智能公司已在国际上闯出了名气。但中国在招募外国研究人员方面仍面临困难。 Jade Gao/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images As the United States and China vie for A.I. dominance, the Trump administration has made it more difficult for companies to hire foreign researchers, while China has made recruiting the world’s best scientists a national priority. 随着美中两国争夺人工智能主导地位，特朗普政府加大了企业雇用外国研究人员的难度，而中国将招募全球顶尖科学家列为国家优先事项。 Over the past two years, China has flung open its doors to international researchers, introducing a visa for scientists and offering lucrative research grants. 过去两年，中国向国际研究人员敞开大门，推出科学家签证，并提供丰厚的研究经费。 Despite those efforts, foreigners are not coming. 然而，尽管作出这些努力，外国人仍没有前来。 Worse still for China’s ambitions, the number of Chinese scientists working in the United States has risen rather than declined, according to a new study about global A.I. research. 对中国雄心而言更糟的是，一项关于全球人工智能研究的新研究显示，在美国工作的中国科学家数量不降反升。 For every 30 Chinese researchers in the United States working on artificial intelligence in 2025, only one in China made the opposite journey, according to the study, conducted by the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, a think tank. 该研究由智库卡内基国际和平研究院开展。结果显示，2025年每30名在美从事人工智能研究的中国研究人员中，只有一人反向前往中国。 “Despite U.S.-China tensions, the number of Chinese-origin researchers working in the U.S. actually rose by four percentage points rather than declined” compared with three years ago, said Damien Ma, who led the study. 领导该研究的马旸表示：“尽管美中关系紧张，但原籍中国的在美研究人员数量实际上没有下降，反而上升了四个百分点。” The study determined the flow of scientists around the world by examining research papers accepted by last year’s NeurIPS, an academic conference focused on machine learning and computational neuroscience. Mr. Ma and his team analyzed where the papers’ authors went to college, received graduate degrees and ended up working. 该研究通过分析去年NeurIPS接收的论文来判断全球科学家的流向。NeurIPS是专注于机器学习和计算神经科学的学术会议。马旸及其团队分析了论文作者就读大学、获得研究生学位以及最终工作的地点。 The results affirm the popular understanding that the United States and China are the two places where most frontier A.I. research is being produced. While China is failing to recruit foreign researchers, the study found, it is seeing a boon in retaining local talent, people who have risen though the domestic education system and are increasingly choosing not to seek work overseas. The United States, on the other hand, maintains its lead by employing foreign researchers, many of whom previously emigrated from China, as well as India, South Korea and elsewhere. 研究结果印证了一个普遍看法：美国和中国产生了大多数前沿人工智能研究。研究发现，中国虽未能招募到外国研究人员，但在留住本土人才方面却大有收获，这些人才通过国内教育体系成长，且越来越倾向于不赴海外工作。另一方面，美国则通过雇用外国研究人员保持领先，其中许多人此前从中国、印度、韩国等地移民而来。 The Carnegie study counts those researchers who migrated from one country to another, but it does not indicate when a researcher moved. One explanation for why the number of Chinese scientists working in America remains high is that they arrived before the Trump administration imposed restrictions on obtaining visas and cut research funding last year. 卡内基的研究统计了从一国迁移至另一国的研究人员，但并未说明迁移时间。在美国工作的中国科学家数量仍居高不下的一个解释是，他们是在特朗普政府去年实施签证限制并削减研究资金之前抵达的。 “There is a delay effect — the researchers in this study mostly made their decisions years ago to study or work here,” said Yingyi Ma, a sociology professor at Syracuse University who studies Asian students in the United States. “The danger for the U.S. is a slow erosion of its appeal to attract talent that compounds over decades. By the time the effect shows up in the data, it is hard to reverse.” “存在延迟效应——本研究中的研究人员大多在多年前就做出了来美学习或工作的决定，”雪城大学研究美国亚洲学生的社会学教授马颖毅说。“美国的危险在于，其对人才的吸引力正缓慢减弱，这种减弱会在数十年间不断累积。等到数据中显现出效果时，就难以逆转了。” For years, Chinese scientists and their peers from around the world were drawn to the United States, which offered career opportunities at start-ups and ample academic funding. But China has gained significant ground in recent years as an alternative for A.I. researchers. 多年来，中国科学家及其世界各地的同行被美国所吸引，因为美国提供初创企业的职业机会和充足的学术资金。但近年来，中国在成为人工智能研究人员的另一个选择方面已取得重大进展。 In 2022, only six of the top 30 institutions publishing papers at NeurIPS were based in China; in 2025, that number rose to 12. Peking University and Tsinghua University, two of China’s top academic institutions, sat at the top of the chart, eclipsing American heavyweights like M.I.T., Stanford and Carnegie Mellon. Chinese researchers also made up 41 percent of the published authors at NeurIPS last year, eclipsing U.S. researchers, who stood at 34 percent. 2022年，在NeurIPS发表论文的前30家机构中，只有六家位于中国；2025年，这一数字升至12家。中国两所顶尖学府北京大学和清华大学位居榜首，超越了麻省理工学院、斯坦福大学和卡内基梅隆大学等重量级美国机构。去年，中国研究人员还占到NeurIPS发表作者的41%，超过美国研究人员的34%。 Today, China has an abundance of workplaces for A.I. researchers, including well-funded universities, big tech companies and start-ups, said Kevin Xu, the founder of Interconnected Capital, a hedge fund that invests in A.I. technologies. As Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Moonshot repeatedly make names for themselves on the global stage, they also become more attractive to top talent. 投资人工智能技术的对冲基金互联资本创始人凯文·徐（音）表示，如今中国拥有大量人工智能研究人员的工作场所，包括资金充足的大学、大型科技公司和初创企业。随着DeepSeek和月之暗面等中国公司在全球舞台上屡屡扬名，它们对顶尖人才的吸引力也日益增强。 “The fact that being able to work at DeepSeek gives you just as much professional prestige and future success as working at OpenAI is quite different from what we’ve observed five years ago, when the path was between working at Google versus Tencent,” Mr. Xu said. “能够在DeepSeek工作所带来的职业声望和未来成功与在OpenAI工作一样，这与我们五年前观察到的情况截然不同，当时人们的选择路径是去谷歌还是去腾讯，”他说。 The ascendancy of Chinese companies might explain why a vast majority of Chinese A.I. researchers choose to remain in the country. But, Mr. Xu added, there’s another reason some researchers remain in China: The government is unwilling to let them go. 中国公司的崛起或许可以解释为何绝大多数中国人工智能研究人员选择留在国内。但凯文·徐补充说，一些研究人员留在中国的另一个原因是：政府不愿放他们走。 This year, the Chinese government restricted the two founders of Manus, an A.I. start-up that was set to be acquired by Meta for $2 billion, from leaving the country. Since then, travel by Chinese A.I. entrepreneurs and researchers — as well as by their spouses and children — has been further curtailed, according to a recent Bloomberg report. 今年，中国政府限制人工智能初创公司Manus的两位创始人出境，该公司原定被Meta以20亿美元收购。据彭博社最近报道，此后，中国人工智能企业家和研究人员——以及其配偶和子女——的出行受到进一步限制。 While China is struggling to recruit foreign talent, it has made some gains in its effort to encourage Chinese researchers and executives abroad to return. 中国在招募外国人才方面困难重重，但在鼓励海外中国研究人员和高管回国方面却取得了一些进展。 The Chinese tech giant Tencent last year appointed Yao Shunyu, a former OpenAI researcher, as its chief A.I. scientist. The move was seen as one of the most notable examples of an A.I. researcher returning to China after having studied and worked in the West. 中国科技巨头腾讯去年任命前OpenAI研究员姚顺雨为其首席人工智能科学家。此举被视为人工智能研究人员在西方学习和工作后回国的最显著例子之一。 Despite China’s new offers of visas and grant money, Silicon Valley still provides more attractive offers and investment opportunities than China for American researchers. Also, moving to a country with few immigrants and a different language is always going to be a challenge. 尽管中国提供了新的签证和经费，但对美国研究人员而言，硅谷仍然给出了比中国更具吸引力的待遇和投资机会。此外，搬到一个移民稀少且语言不同的国家始终是一项挑战。 “For everybody else who’s outside the walled garden, culturally or digitally, it’s still very hard to break into,” Mr. Xu said. “对于围墙花园之外的其他人来说，无论是文化上还是数字上，仍然很难闯入，”凯文·徐说。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 中国人之间为何彼此怨恨、互相攻击？
items.description: 高雨莘2026年10月8日 Matt Rota For years, the mood in China has been darkening. 多年来，中国的社会情绪日益沉郁。 A weakening economy has left many disillusioned, a state of mind expressed privately and across the heavily controlled internet in lowered expectations and quiet anxiety. 经济疲软令许多人深感幻灭。在私下交流及受到严格管控的互联网上，这种心境通过不断降低的期望和默默的焦虑表现出来。 Some of that may now be surfacing in more troubling ways. 如今，部分此类情绪可能正以更令人不安的方式浮出水面。 In March, a man drove a heavy construction vehicle through an outdoor market in a Beijing suburb, reportedly killing several people. In June, a small aircraft crashed into a prominent office building in the capital, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others in what may have been a suicide. And last month a man was arrested in the southern city of Guangzhou after allegedly slashing the faces of multiple women in a busy shopping district. 今年3月，一名男子在北京市郊的一个露天市场驾驶重型工程车冲撞人群，据报道造成数人死亡。6月，一架小型飞机在首都撞向一栋知名办公楼，致使飞行员死亡及另外13人受伤，可能是一起自杀事件。上个月在南方城市广州，一名男子因涉嫌在繁华商业区划伤多名女性面部而被捕。 Incidents like these are rare in China and heavily censored, making motives difficult, if not impossible, to discern. But in a country where it’s dangerous to vent at government policies, I can’t shake the sense that people are instead beginning to take their anger and frustration out on one another. 此类事件在中国十分罕见且受到严格审查，因此很难（即便并非不可能）查明其动机。然而，在一个发泄对政府政策的不满会面临危险的国家，我产生了一种挥之不去的感觉：人们正开始将愤怒与挫败感发泄在彼此身上。 Intensely focused on competing with the United States, Beijing is pouring resources into building up its advanced manufacturing and technology industries, seeing them as the future drivers of national growth. During a summit meeting with President Trump at the White House last week, President Xi Jinping of China spoke confidently, saying China was “breaking new ground” in his modernization drive. 聚焦于中美竞争的北京正投入大量资源发展先进制造业和科技产业，将其视为国家经济增长的未来引擎。上周在白宫与特朗普总统举行峰会期间，中国国家主席习近平满怀信心地表示，中国正在其现代化进程中“开辟新天地”。 But much of the broader economy remains weak. Unemployment is high, especially for younger people, and wages are stagnating. Households still reeling from the long-term collapse of the country’s real estate market are cutting back on spending. The government this year set its lowest annual growth target since 1991. 但更广泛的经济领域大多依然疲软。失业率居高不下（尤其是年轻人），工资水平停滞不前。众多家庭仍因本国房地产市场的长期崩盘而步履维艰，正纷纷削减开支。今年，政府设定了自1991年以来的最低年度经济增长目标。 The impulse to find someone to blame is clearly evident in the viral doxxing phenomenon called “ba,” or “to strip.” In these campaigns, which have intensified in recent months, posses of digital sleuths comb through the backgrounds of people who have attracted attention for their academic or professional achievements, “stripping” them down in a hunt for evidence that connections, fraud or favoritism paved their way. 急于找人承担罪责的冲动，在被称为“扒”（即“剥去”）的病毒式人肉搜索现象中体现得淋漓尽致。近几个月来此类运动愈演愈烈，成群结队的“网络侦探”对那些因学术或事业成就而备受瞩目之人进行事无巨细的背景调查，将他们“扒”个干干净净，试图寻找靠关系、造假或偏袒来取得成功的证据。 In late July, a 29-year-old podcaster named Zhuge Yiyang — a Ph.D. candidate at Boston College — went viral after she interviewed the director Christopher Nolan about his movie “The Odyssey.” Ms. Zhuge had been admired by many of her online followers as proof that hard work and merit lead to success, and she was widely praised for the intellectual depth of her questions in the interview. 7月下旬，一位名叫诸葛一杨的29岁博主——波士顿学院博士候选人——在就电影《奥德赛》采访导演克里斯托弗·诺兰后走红。她在网上的众多粉丝以她为努力与实力造就成功的表率，她在采访中所提问题的思想深度也广受赞誉。 Soon, however, the online stripping started, leading to accusations that she had plagiarized material in her podcasts and writing. Ms. Zhuge has disputed some of the accusations, but canceled public appearances and described herself as emotionally exhausted. 然而不久之后，网络上的“深扒”接踵而至，引发了对其播客和文章素材存在抄袭的指控。诸葛女士对部分指控予以反驳，但取消了公开露面，并称自己已身心俱疲。 Often, the scrutiny seems less about exposing wrongdoing than about a reflexive resentment of perceived elites who have become avatars of an economy in which many people see their own prospects narrowing. Other recent targets have ranged from a Chinese actress to prominent doctors and a Harvard graduate who last year became the first Chinese woman to speak at a commencement ceremony at the university. The young woman called for global unity in her speech but was soon accused of using family privilege and connections to further her academic career. 通常，这种审视与其说是在揭露不当行为，不如说是在条件反射式地怨恨那些被视为精英的人——在许多人看来，这些精英已成为一种经济的化身，而他们自己的前景在这种经济中正变得越来越窄。近期遭遇针对的其他目标涵盖了一名女演员、多位知名医生，以及一名去年成为首位在哈佛大学毕业典礼上致辞的中国籍女性的哈佛毕业生。她在演讲中呼吁全球团结，但很快就被指控利用家族特权和关系来助推其学术生涯。 Fraud, nepotism and plagiarism are hardly new in China, nor is the tendency for people to take aim at perceived inequities online. What feels new is how automatic and ferocious the hunt for them has become as sensitivity rises over who gets ahead — and how — at a time of pervasive economic anxiety. 欺诈、裙带关系和抄袭在中国绝非新鲜事，网民将矛头对准其认为的不公现象亦是如此。真正让人感到新鲜的是，在普遍存在经济焦虑的当下，随着人们对“谁能出人头地以及如何出人头地”的敏感度不断上升，这种“扒”变得如此自动化且来势汹汹。 Bitterness is intensifying between men and women, too. In online forums, men complain that more of the pressure from the worsening economic prospects falls on them. They rail against feminists, and some have even called for a men’s rights awakening. 男女两性之间的对立与怨恨也在加剧。在网络论坛上，男性抱怨经济前景恶化所带来的更多压力落在了他们肩上。他们强烈抨击女权主义者，部分人甚至呼吁男性权利意识的觉醒。 Male frustration spilled into the streets in August when groups of young men, apparently protesting the effeminizing of youth culture, reportedly gathered in the city of Chongqing outside the office of a talent agency that handled boy bands. After police detained one of the men, the protesters marched down a major road, demanding his release and chasing, shoving and kicking female fans waiting outside the agency. Some took photos of the women, which were digitally altered as pornographic images and disseminated online. 这种男性的挫败感在8月份蔓延到了街头。据报道，为抗议青年文化的“女性化”倾向，一群群年轻男子聚集在重庆一家管理男子偶像团体的经纪公司办公室外。在警方拘留其中一名男子后，抗议者在主干道上游行要求放人，并对在经纪公司外等候的女粉丝进行追逐、推搡和踢打。部分人还拍下这些女性的照片，用数字技术篡改成色情图像并在网上散播。 Studies suggest that many Chinese men, particularly those with fewer resources, face mounting difficulty fulfilling traditional expectations to marry and become stable breadwinners. A man is often expected to have an apartment and a car before he can secure a wife. For many, that’s becoming nearly impossible. 研究表明，许多中国男性（尤其是资源较匮乏者）在满足“结婚并成为稳定养家者”的传统期望方面，正面临越来越大的困难。社会通常期望男性在娶妻前必须拥有住房和汽车。对许多人而言，这正变得几乎遥不可及。 In some parts of the country, a groom’s family may also be expected to pay a “bride price,” a payment to the bride’s family as part of the marriage agreement. A survey of young male migrant workers, which was published in February, put the average price at around 130,000 yuan ($19,000) — about six times the respondents’ average annual savings. 在部分地区，新郎的家庭还可能被要求支付“彩礼”（作为婚姻协议一部分付给女方家庭的钱款）。今年2月公布的一项针对年轻男性农民工的调查显示，平均彩礼金额约为13万元人民币——大约是受访者平均年积蓄的六倍。 Marriage prospects are worsened by the government’s former one-child policy which, combined with a traditional preference for male heirs, led many families to abort female fetuses, skewing China’s gender balance. The policy was ended a decade ago, but single men of marriageable age outnumbered unwed women by as much as two to one in some parts of the country, according to the most recent detailed census in 2020. Last year, China still had nearly 29 million more men than women. 昔日的独生子女政策进一步恶化了婚姻前景，该政策加上重男轻女的传统观念导致许多家庭选择堕掉女胎，从而造成中国性别比例失衡。尽管该政策已于十年前废止，但根据2020年最新一次详尽的人口普查，在部分地区，适婚单身男性与未婚女性的比例高达二比一。去年，中国男性总数依然比女性多出近2900万。 I grew up in a China whose ascent was powered not just by factories, investment and growing incomes, but by the sense that all boats were rising. Even if some rose faster, people could see those who had made it and imagine joining their ranks. They could look forward to building families and bringing up children whose lives would be better than their own. 在我儿时的中国，推动其崛起的不仅有工厂、投资和不断增长的收入，还有一种“水涨船高”的普遍感受。即使部分人致富速度更快，人们也能看到那些成功者，并憧憬着加入他们的行列。他们期待着成家立业，抚养生活注定会比自己更好的下一代。 What’s disturbing about China today is not simply that those expectations are fading, but that success itself is cause for suspicion and outright hostility: If I am falling behind, someone else must be getting ahead at my expense; if I can’t meet the expectations society places on men, a woman must be to blame. 当今中国令人不安的不仅在于这些期望正在破灭，更在于“成功”本身成了遭受怀疑和公然敌视的理由：如果我落后了，必定是别人踩着我的利益往上爬；如果我无法满足社会对男性的期望，那错的一定是女人。 The Chinese state has enormous power to steer the economy and shape public life. What it cannot simply command back into existence is goodwill between its citizens. 中国政府拥有掌控经济和塑造公共生活的巨大权力。但它无法仅凭一道命令就让国民之间的善意失而复得。 Economic downturns end. A fraying social fabric may prove harder to mend. 经济衰退终会结束。但修补不断磨损的社会结构恐将困难得多。 高雨莘(Helen Gao)是一名自由撰稿人，常驻北京。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

They could look forward to building families and bringing up children whose lives would be better than their own. 在我儿时的中国，推动其崛起的不仅有工厂、投资和不断增长的收入，还有一种“水涨船高”的普遍感受。即使部分人致富速度更快，人们也能看到那些成功者，并憧憬着加入他们的行列。他们期待着成家立业，抚养生活注定会比自己更好的下一代。 What’s disturbing about China today is not simply that those expectations are fading, but that success itself is cause for suspicion and outright hostility: If I am falling behind, someone else must be getting ahead at my expense; if I can’t meet the expectations society places on men, a woman must be to blame. 当今中国令人不安的不仅在于这些期望正在破灭，更在于“成功”本身成了遭受怀疑和公然敌视的理由：如果我落后了，必定是别人踩着我的利益往上爬；如果我无法满足社会对男性的期望，那错的一定是女人。 The Chinese state has enormous power to steer the economy and shape public life. What it cannot simply command back into existence is goodwill between its citizens. 中国政府拥有掌控经济和塑造公共生活的巨大权力。但它无法仅凭一道命令就让国民之间的善意失而复得。 Economic downturns end. A fraying social fabric may prove harder to mend. 经济衰退终会结束。但修补不断磨损的社会结构恐将困难得多。 高雨莘(Helen Gao)是一名自由撰稿人，常驻北京。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries. https://rea.tools English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Türkçe · Русский · Tiếng Việt · ไทย · Deutsch · Español · Français · Українська · Polski · Português (Brasil) · العربية · فارسی REA: Reverse Engineer Anything One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior. See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level. Website · Guides · Showcases Quick start · How REA works · What you can analyze · Showcases · FAQ · Documentation npx rea-agents setup Join the Reverse Engineering Community Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. Visit the REA website for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies. Quick start Set up your agent With Node.js and npm installed, run: npx rea-agents setup Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and other agents. See installation and setup for provider configuration and manual MCP registration. Ask your agent Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. Use the terminal Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as "D:/apps/example" on Windows. To install the rea command for regular use: npm install --global rea-agents rea --help For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the CLI and Evidence guide for native commands, provider selection, snapshots and scripting. Update REA REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your installation up to date. For an npm-installed CLI: rea update To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed by the update. If you use npx, update your agent setup with: npx rea-agents@latest setup Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands, use npx rea-agents@latest followed by the command. How REA works Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code. REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation. CLI commands use the same workflows. Open the full-size figure. What you can analyze REA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.19), 24.x (>=24.11), or 26+, plus npm. Additional tools and host support depend on the target: Target What REA returns Requirements and guide Native binaries Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references Hopper, Ghidra or IDA; native analysis Offline ELF layout Sections, segments, original symbols/relocations and static mitigation candidates Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; binary diagnostics EVM bytecode Dispatch selectors, byte offsets, inferred arguments and mutability Local raw/hex carrier; offline EVM guide Recorded Linux crashes Raw notes, every recorded thread's registers/signals and optional mapping candidates Caller-supplied pwntools; optional GDB/pwndbg; recorded crashes JavaScript / Electron Modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC and native add-on relationships Node.js and npm; application analysis Websites Page structure, scripts, network observations and requested screenshots A Chrome-family browser; browser analysis Saved network captures Requests, responses, exposed payloads and source locations HAR; mitmdump on Linux for native mitmproxy captures; capture guide .NET assemblies Metadata, CIL instructions, declared native dependencies and build comparisons None (static only); managed-code guide Android APKs Manifest declarations, classes, decompiled methods and references Headless JADX and a full JDK on Linux/macOS/Windows x64; Android guide Firmware Regions, extraction results and native-analysis handoffs Binwalk / Unblob on Linux; firmware guide Packages and resources File inventories, digests, plists, Apple bundle anatomy and extracted resources Artifact and JavaScript guide, Apple applications Process behavior Terminal output, interactions, exit and filesystem observations, and run comparisons Linux/macOS with a native PTY; process capture Static JavaScript and .NET inspection read the supplied files without running the application. Runtime capture runs or interacts with the selected target using your user permissions; each runtime guide describes its effects. Native formats and host support vary by provider. See Hopper and Ghidra setup, the IDA guide, and experimental Windows Ghidra support. Ghidra also supports 16-bit DOS analysis. For large binaries, raise its startup deadline with REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS. For provider selection, see the CLI guide. Check release availability for features added since the latest npm release. Showcases DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation Follow a sound call into its position-to-pan helper, inspect the instructions, and turn incomplete pseudocode into C. The reconstruction passes 3,205 original-x86 cases and reproduces all 63 compiled function bytes. Read the case study · Reconstruction repository Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge Find the renderer's clipboard API, follow it through preload and IPC into the main process, and inspect the rich clipboard format. Read the case study TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation Inspect the original PC-98 game's 16-bit instructions, recover the fixed and aimed angle calculations, and compare the reconstructed C++ with the historical compiler output. Read the case study · Reconstruction repository If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an issue or a pull request, including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. FAQ Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the supported agents; other clients can use manual MCP registration. Do I need Hopper, Ghidra or IDA? Deep native analysis uses one of them. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra and IDA use your existing installations. See provider setup. Do I need to start Hopper first? REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. See Hopper startup and troubleshooting. What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use npx rea-agents setup to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See skill-only installation. What code does REA return? Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the showcases give worked examples. Does REA upload my app? REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy. What should I do if I hit a bug? Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For an npm-installed CLI: rea update For agent setup through npx: npx rea-agents@latest setup If you're using an agent, complete the setup refresh and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, open an issue with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output. Documentation Start with the website's worked guides. For exact options, prerequisites and result contracts: Installation and setup: agent registration, provider configuration, updates and uninstall. Readiness and troubleshooting: diagnose one agent or analysis engine. CLI and Evidence: commands, provider selection, snapshots, import/export and exit statuses. MCP contracts and agent prompts: tool results, sessions and guided investigations. Tool catalog: generated inventory of tools, providers and CLI commands. Roadmap: planned work and capability trackers. Report vulnerabilities through SECURITY.md. Star history 🎉 50,000 GitHub stars — thank you! Thanks to everyone using REA, reporting bugs, requesting features, testing builds, and contributing fixes. Disclaimer REA provides tools for lawful reverse-engineering research, analysis, and reconstruction. You are responsible for obtaining any required authorization and complying with applicable laws. The project does not endorse illegal or unauthorized use. REA is an open-source software project. We have not issued or endorsed any cryptocurrency or token. Tokens using the REA name are not affiliated with the project. Contributing We'd love your help with REA! Open an issue to report a bug or suggest a feature, or send a pull request to improve the code or docs. See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup and checks, testing for verification lanes, and the architecture map for the project structure. License MIT

items.title: boykopovar/AnyPS5
items.description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows https://discord.gg/BHFztBPUe About Tool for automatic executables porting to Linux and Windows. Includes a relinker that converts executable to the target system's native format and implementations of system prx libraries suitable for dynamic linking. No emulation or separate runtime process. Usage, Build instructions, Architecture, Technical debt of the project, code style conventions, contributing Status * System libraries: percentage of the functions known to the project so far (declared in core/libs/prx), not of every PS5 system function. The total grows as more functions are declared. List of verified games Dreaming Sarah (2D platformer) runs at a stable 60 fps on a GTX 1050 Ti / i5-7500 3.4GHz. Unsupported or unexpected states strictly throw std::runtime_error. what() is printed to stderr and the process terminates. The shader recompiler successfully produces SPIR-V (validated via Spirv-Tools when built with ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS). Compatibility See the game compatibility list for tested games and known issues. Input mapping SDL-mapped game controllers are supported, including analog sticks and triggers. Keyboard and mouse controls can be configured with an anyps5-input.ini file. See input mapping for the supported devices and configuration format. Disclaimer This project is intended for interoperability, research, preservation, and compatibility purposes. It does not include, distribute, or require copyrighted software, firmware, cryptographic keys, or proprietary libraries. Users are responsible for ensuring that any binaries used with this project are obtained and used in accordance with applicable laws and their respective license terms. items.title: mattpocock/skills
items.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory. https://aihero.dev/skills Skills For Real Engineers My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy. If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter: Sign Up To The Newsletter Installation (30-second setup) A plugin updates itself. skills.sh copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice. 1. Get the skills Claude Code claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official Updates itself by default. Codex codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock Updates itself at startup. GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code) copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock Then, once, add to ~/.copilot/settings.json: { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "mattpocock": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "mattpocock/skills" }, "autoUpdate": true } } } In VS Code, run Chat: Install Plugin From Source and enter https://github.com/mattpocock/skills. It updates daily. Gemini CLI (manual updates) gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity Re-run both commands to update. Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates) npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose When the installer asks which skills to take, include setup-matt-pocock-skills. To update, run npx skills@latest update, and re-run add to pick up new skills. 2. Run /setup-matt-pocock-skills In your agent, run it once per repo. It will: Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe) Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them (/triage uses labels) Ask you where you want to save any docs we create 3. Bam - you're ready to go. Why These Skills Exist I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want "No-one knows exactly what they want" David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, The Pragmatic Programmer The Problem. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all. This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a grilling session - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building. The Fix is to use: /grill-me - for non-code uses /grill-with-docs - same as /grill-me, but adds more goodies (see below) These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them every time you want to make a change. #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model. Eric Evans, Domain-Driven-Design The Problem: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages. I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do. The Fix for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project. Example Here's an example glossary (still named CONTEXT.md at that pinned commit, from before the skills renamed the convention), from my course-video-manager repo. Which one is easier to read? BEFORE: "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)" AFTER: "There's a problem with the materialization cascade" This concision pays off session after session. This is built into /grill-with-docs. It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's. It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see. Tip A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity: Variables, functions and files are named consistently, using the shared language As a result, the codebase is easier to navigate for the agent The agent also spends fewer tokens on thinking, because it has access to a more concise language #3: The Code Doesn't Work "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big." David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, The Pragmatic Programmer The Problem: Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent still produces crap? It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind. The Fix: You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests. For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code. I've built a /tdd skill you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests. For debugging, I've also built a /diagnosing-bugs skill that wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase. #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud "Invest in the design of the system every day." Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface." John Ousterhout, A Philosophy Of Software Design The Problem: Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate. The Fix for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code. This is built in to every layer of these skills: /to-spec quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a spec And crucially, /improve-codebase-architecture surveys a codebase for deepening opportunities and hands you the candidates. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you. Summary Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy. Reference These split on one axis: who can invoke them. User-invoked skills are reachable only when you type them (e.g. /grill-me); their job is to orchestrate. Model-invoked skills can be invoked by you or reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits; they hold the reusable discipline.
